players.product: York chillers for hyperscale data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q1 2026 results, which CEO Joakim Weidemanis said 'delivered ahead of expectations': organic revenue grew 6% with broad-based contribution across the portfolio, led by service, which grew 9% year over year. By region, Americas sales were up 6% organically (solid double-digit growth in service), EMEA grew 4% and APAC delivered 8% growth led by strong system performance, against a challenging 10% year-over-year comparison. Segment margins increased 70 basis points to 15.7% and adjusted EBIT margin expanded 190 basis points to 12.4%, on productivity, price realization and a better cost structure. Adjusted segment EBITDA margins were 16.4% in the Americas (+20 basis points), 13.5% in EMEA (+120 basis points) and 16.9% in APAC (+290 basis points). Adjusted EPS of $0.89 rose nearly 40% year over year and beat guidance. The quarter ended with approximately $600 million in available cash, and net debt fell to 2.2 times, within the long-term target range.
quarterly_data.figure: organic revenue grew 6%; adjusted EBIT margin 12.4% (+190 basis points); adjusted EPS of $0.89 (up nearly 40%)

quarterly_data.signal: Orders grew nearly 40% in fiscal Q1 2026, on top of a tough 16% compare, and backlog hit a record: 'Our record backlog grew 20% to $18 billion'. CFO Marc Vandiepenbeeck said 'Demand was led by data centers projects where customers are accelerating investment to support higher density workloads and AI-driven growth.' By region, the Americas delivered 56% order growth 'led by large-scale data center projects that continue to scale across the region'; EMEA orders grew 8% and APAC orders 10%. The CEO stressed that data centers are not the only driver: life science orders were very healthy because pharmaceutical makers are building new biologics plants. He added that many of the larger data center and life science orders 'are not necessarily shippable, you know, within the next nine months or so.' The CFO said all of the backlog could ship in the next twelve months, but conversion depends on how fast customers can accept deliveries, so it still supports only the mid-single-digit revenue guide. He said that looking past twelve months, the backlog would let management start talking about 'a slightly better growth'.
quarterly_data.figure: orders increased nearly 40%; Americas delivered 56% growth; record backlog grew 20% to $18 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance at the fiscal Q1 2026 call. For fiscal Q2: organic sales growth of approximately 5%, operating leverage of approximately 45% and adjusted EPS of approximately $1.11. For full-year fiscal 2026: organic sales growth held at mid-single digits, backed by backlog visibility (the CFO said the year started in the lower part of that range and the second half should land in the better half); operating leverage of approximately 50% as last year's stranded-cost savings come through; and adjusted EPS guidance RAISED to approximately $4.70 per share, roughly 25% growth, with approximately 100% free cash flow conversion. The CFO said any faster top-line growth would carry operating leverage closer to the long-term algorithm, 'well above 30%', rather than the 50% range.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 adjusted EPS approximately $1.11; FY2026 adjusted EPS raised to approximately $4.70 per share (roughly 25% growth); FY organic sales growth of mid-single digits

quarterly_data.signal: Data center chiller launches introduced 'earlier this week', at 'the big show that's ongoing as we speak'. The YDAM 'delivers up to 3.5 megawatts of cooling in a compact footprint, providing approximately 20% higher capacity density than competing options and enabling warm water cooling for advanced GPUs'. The YKHT offers 'the industry's widest operating range and supports waterless heat reduction, which can eliminate up to 9 million gallons of cooling tower water annually in typical deployments'. The Smart Ready Chiller provides '10 times the insights over a standard remote connected chiller', which management expects to move more customers into recurring service. JCI also released a new reference guide that 'maps the full thermal chain and outlines scalable high-performance cooling architectures for an emerging class of AI factories'. CEO Joakim Weidemanis said 'We continue to work closely with NVIDIA' and that some of the guides 'is in collaboration with NVIDIA'. An analyst asked about the technology path, noting investor worry over NVIDIA and warm water cooling. The CEO would not comment on future launches but said there is 'a significant roadmap behind that'. He said the new products' effect on orders so far is 'very minor' ('it's more about what's to come') and that he expects them to start lifting orders in the current quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: YDAM up to 3.5 megawatts of cooling with approximately 20% higher capacity density; YKHT can eliminate up to 9 million gallons of cooling tower water annually

quarterly_data.signal: Data center thermal portfolio, per CEO Joakim Weidemanis. JCI plays in three categories plus controls: chillers; CRAHs (transcribed as 'craws') and air handling units 'through our silent air franchise, which is the leading franchise in air handling'; and CDUs. JCI entered the CDU space 'a couple of quarters ago' and is 'now starting to grow nicely here on the CDU side'. CDU sales today are 'a mix': plenty of business is CDUs only, but JCI sees 'plenty of opportunity for combined offers' with key accounts. As data center thermal architecture evolves, 'the roles that certain devices play today might evolve', which is why JCI added CDUs. Customer mix: JCI historically had a good position with hyperscalers and many large colos in the United States. Growth in Europe and Asia has now become 'very meaningful', and more future growth will come from Asia Pac and Europe, where the mix of hyperscalers and local colos is a little different, so 'our data center business is gonna broaden'. Countries in Southeast Asia and India are looking at data centers, with several emerging players. The CEO saw no material change in how the big hyperscaler and colo players behave. Every other week, large engineering teams from JCI's largest customers, colos and hyperscalers, work with JCI engineers at its JADEC innovation center in Pennsylvania on next-generation designs, and that work feeds the product roadmap.

Capacity and delivery help win data center orders. Plant and machinery investments made before CEO Joakim Weidemanis joined 'more than tripled our physical capacity' across chillers and air handling units; the air-handling investment also 'made room for the CDU business'. That fixed cost has been in the run rate for more than a year, so added volume creates leverage. Lean work can keep expanding capacity 'materially, very materially' without spending the same amount of capital. At one key chiller factory, on-time delivery went from 95% to sustaining 95 to 100% for the past couple of months. Lead times were earlier cut in half for one product line, and that work is being cascaded to other lines and factories. The CEO said JCI's 'now competitively advantaged lead times is driving higher win rates with our customers, especially in data centers'. He said there are 'no major bottlenecks at this point in time' in scaling larger orders and no particular margin headwind from them. The CFO said 'we don't believe we've reached that capacity constraint just yet'. Large customers ordering for several planned data centers weigh a vendor's ability to deliver and to react quickly.
quarterly_data.figure: physical capacity more than tripled; chiller factory on-time delivery went from 95% to sustaining 95 to 100%; lead times cut in half for one product line
